text:
sam: FYI seeing sustained throughput drop on pool `pool-nyc-dedicated-3` starting ~03:10 UTC. 35% lower p95 output tokens, customers report tail latency and 429s. example request_id=rid_8a2f

olivia: ugh. any recent config pushes to batching/dispatcher?

alex: nothing on infra pushed in last 2h from my side. but I saw autoscale churn around 03:08 in the logs. link to traces: https://internal/trace/rid_8a2f (permissioned)

maya: adding quick dump of queue stats from the node that hit 90% load:
```
queue_depth: 124
avg_batch_size_tokens: 280
avg_batch_size_requests: 1.7
batch_window_ms: 30
continuous_batcher_pending: 63
KV_cache_hit_rate: 0.22
```

sam: those numbers look like tiny request packing. avg tokens low -> inefficient GPU utilization. suspect `continuous-batcher` falling back to microbatches.

juan: I grabbed a scheduler snapshot: a recent change to adaptive batching weight landed in canary at 02:55. It reduces max_wait for low-priority tenants when busy. Could cause more prefill drains.

olivia: can we repro locally? steps I ran:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer x" -d '{"input":"long prompt..."}' https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "X-Tenant: tenant-42"
2) hit with 200 rps sustained for 10m
observed queue fragmentation around 03:05 in local sim (see logs)

alex: repro confirmed in staging with `tenant-42` traffic shape. I see many single-request microbatches: `batcher.emit(size=1,tokens=30)`. Looks like the adaptive heuristic is choosing latency over pack efficiency during spikes.

sam: can we toggle back the heuristic? who owns the adaptive-batcher flag?

maya: flag is `adaptive.batch_priority_v2`. I can flip to previous behavior for the pool. will do a quick canary rollback to the old heuristic on one shard.

deploy-bot: deploy started by maya: rollback adaptive.batch_priority_v2 -> v1 on pool-nyc-dedicated-3/shard-7. Job: deploy-4739.

alex: after rollback, initial signs look good: avg_batch_size_requests jumped to 3.8, avg_batch_size_tokens 920, queue_depth dropped 60% in 90s.

juan: watchers: check autoscale too. if batching efficiency increases, we should avoid unnecessary scale-ups. but there was a flapping event earlier.

sam: customers still saw some 429s during the window. need a postmortem with timeline (config change, autoscale churn, degraded packing).

olivia: logging note: include `batch_window_ms`, `avg_batch_tokens`, `tenant_priority` in per-request traces to help future debugging. created ticket: https://issues/RED-7821

maya: rolled back fully on pool-nyc-dedicated-3. monitoring dashboard shows throughput recovering to baseline over next 3m.

sre-bot: Alert resolved: throughput-drop-pool-nyc-dedicated-3 at 2765432160.

sam: thanks all. next actions: 1) revert adaptive change and run canary longer with synthetic tenant shapes, 2) add telemetry for microbatch rates, 3) evaluate safer defaults for `max_batch_tokens` and `min_batch_requests`. I'll coordinate with product on opt-in for small-tenant latency profile. :thumbsup:
